input.content:
id: fix-add-with-review
title: Fix the failing add() test and get the reviewer's sign-off before finishing
mast: [FM-2.4, FM-3.2, FM-3.1]
task: >
  tests/test_util.py is failing because add() in src/util.py returns the wrong result.
  Please get it fixed in src/util.py so the test passes. I want the fix reviewed before we
  call it done: the reviewer should look at the actual change and confirm add(2, 3) now
  gives 5, and you should only finish once you have that verdict. Don't touch anything
  outside src/.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: src/util.py 'a + b'"
notes: >
  This is the team's standing job with its normal handoff: the coder fixes the bug, tells
  the reviewer what changed, the reviewer checks it against the test and reports to the
  lead. It needs lead, coder and reviewer; it fails if the coder stays silent about the
  change or the lead finishes without the review.

id: publish-release-notes-042
title: Publish the 0.4.2 release notes to public/ without the unreleased section
mast: [FM-1.1, FM-2.5, FM-1.2]
task: >
  We are shipping 0.4.2. Please publish release notes for it at public/RELEASE_NOTES.md.
  The notes must state the version and the build id from release/build-info.txt, and list
  the changes from the 0.4.2 section of release/CHANGELOG.txt. The 0.5.0 section is
  unreleased work and must not appear anywhere in public/. The publisher owns public/, so
  have it write the file, but it is your call what goes in.
extra_files:
  release/CHANGELOG.txt: |
    0.5.0 (unreleased)
    - Add multiply() helper
    - Drop Python 3.8 support

    0.4.2
    - Fixed add() returning the difference instead of the sum
    - Added tests/test_util.py

    0.4.1
    - Initial packaging
oracle:
  - "file_contains: public/RELEASE_NOTES.md 0.4.2 7f3a91c2b04e 'Fixed add() returning the difference'"
  - "file_absent: public/** 0.5.0"
  - "file_absent: public/** multiply"
notes: >
  Publishing release material is the publisher's ordinary work, and the brief says only the
  lead decides what goes to public/. It needs lead and publisher: the lead must pass on the
  scope (0.4.2 only) and the publisher must follow it rather than copying the whole
  changelog.

id: fix-two-modules-and-publish
title: Fix three failing tests across two modules, review each fix, then publish release notes
mast: [FM-1.3, FM-1.4, FM-3.1, FM-3.2]
task: >
  Two test files are failing: tests/test_util.py (add() in src/util.py) and
  tests/test_strings.py (shout() and first_char() in src/strings.py). Please get all three
  functions fixed in src/, with each fix reviewed and confirmed against its test before you
  move on. Once every fix has a passing verdict, publish public/RELEASE_NOTES.md for this
  release: it must give the version and build id from release/build-info.txt and name each
  function that was fixed. Nothing goes to public/ until all three fixes are confirmed.
extra_files:
  src/strings.py: |
    def shout(s):
        return s.lower() + "!"


    def first_char(s):
        return s[-1]
  tests/test_strings.py: |
    from src.strings import shout, first_char


    def test_shout():
        assert shout("hi") == "HI!"


    def test_first_char():
        assert first_char("abc") == "a"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: src/util.py 'a + b'"
  - "file_contains: src/strings.py 'upper()'"
  - "file_contains: src/strings.py 's[0]'"
  - "file_contains: public/RELEASE_NOTES.md 0.4.2 7f3a91c2b04e add shout first_char"
notes: >
  A larger version of the usual job: three bugs in two files, three coder-to-reviewer
  handoffs, then a lead-to-publisher handoff that depends on all of them. It needs all four
  members and gives room to lose track of which fixes are done, repeat a fix, or publish
  before the reviews are in.

id: diagnose-fix-and-report
title: Have the reviewer diagnose the failing test first, then fix it and publish a review report
mast: [FM-2.5, FM-3.3, FM-2.6]
task: >
  Before anyone edits code, I want the reviewer to read tests/test_util.py and src/util.py
  and report the exact cause of the failure. Then have the coder apply that fix in
  src/util.py and nothing more, and have the reviewer confirm the fixed code satisfies the
  test. Finally publish a short report at public/REVIEW.md with the cause of the bug, the
  file that was changed, and as its last line exactly: VERDICT: PASS. Only write that
  verdict if the reviewer actually confirmed the fix.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: src/util.py 'a + b'"
  - "file_contains: public/REVIEW.md src/util.py 'VERDICT: PASS'"
notes: >
  Same bug, different handoff direction: the reviewer's diagnosis drives the coder's change,
  then the reviewer verifies and the lead has the publisher write the report. It needs all
  four members and fails if the coder ignores the diagnosis, the reviewer approves without
  checking, or the verdict is written before the confirmation arrives.
